Look at Fig. 15 and you'll see it right away: the alitrunk is swollen, and it sits much higher than the propodeal dorsum. The propodeum carries a pair of strong spines, straight to slightly upcurved. There's no metanotal groove. The metapleural lobes are triangular and conspicuous.

Now turn to the petiole in profile. It has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node whose dorsum slopes down posteriorly, which leaves a short posterior face. On the postpetiole, the anterior and dorsal surfaces run together in a single convexity, and the posterior face is truncated. In dorsal view, the nodes of petiole and postpetiole are both broader than long.

The head tells you more. Its dorsum is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye-level. Those rugae wander a little and are irregular, and a few anastomoses are usually present. The scrobal area is mostly smooth, though you'll usually find 1–2 fine rugulae crossing its width just behind the antennal fossa. Behind the eyes, the sides of the head are finely reticulate-rugose, and that sculpture runs around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. Between the rugae, the spaces are unsculptured, or at most show faint superficial traces.

The dorsal alitrunk is finely but strongly reticulate-rugose everywhere, with broad shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose; the postpetiole ranges from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured. Every dorsal surface of head and body is densely clothed with fine, acute hairs. Color runs from dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

UPO-06: PrhI Gene Synthesis
UPO-06 carries the coding sequence for *Ralstonia solanacearum* prhI, an ECF sigma factor you need for transcription driven by the Prh signal transduction system. PrhR switches the gene on, and it then directs sigma factor expression through activation of the PprhJ promoter. We optimized the sequence for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

UPO-11: PprhJ Promoter Synthesis
UPO-11 gives you the PprhJ promoter region. It responds to plant cell contact through signal transduction mediated by PrhA and PrhR, and the ECF sigma factor PrhI activates it. We optimized the sequence for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

Subject: Key Findings on foxl2 Expression Patterns in Trout

Dear Customer,

Here is what we found about foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both transcripts were expressed very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a stayed highly restricted in the male. The diverged paralog foxl2b, however, showed up in most adult extragonadal tissues we examined (see Additional file 2).

In adult females, foxl2b was confined almost entirely to the skin, gill, and ovary. In the testis, its expression was very strong. That fits with earlier findings showing foxl2b present while foxl2a is absent in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Put together, these results point to foxl2b as a likely regulator of male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), especially later in development.

Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) cannot support carbon neutrality claims for electrical use beyond a claimant's metered consumption, because most RECs come from projects that would have been financially viable without their sale. [10] Consequently, they lack additionality. Additionality asks a counterfactual question: what would have happened under the status quo if the REC had never been purchased or contracted? There are many frameworks for testing additionality, but the core question stays the same: did the project need REC revenues to survive financially? Without verified proof of additionality, RECs cannot be treated as genuine emissions offsets.

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation from the formal work of Smith & Sprinks (1975), then used it to get a higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Here is what matters most: using only the linear dispersion relation for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). The leading-order solution shows the modified curvature terms of the MMSE matter, while the slope square terms stay negligible, as the mild-slope assumption predicts. So we kept every modified curvature term the MSE drops, and that gave us a uniform model.

To test it, we built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM) that predicts wave scattering over a varying bottom. The uniform model captures the main features of waves over different sea beds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, it matches the experimental data more closely than other established models. For man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model beat the results of Kirby (1986) against the same data.

One more thing worth knowing: the FEM model also handles the transformation of waves over arbitrarily-varying bathymetry.

MapleStory Monsters: A Survival Guide to the Underworld

Welcome to MapleStory. There are thousands of monsters roaming the world, so here is a quick breakdown of where they live and how to survive.

The weak monsters are the most common foes, and you will find them by towns. They wander aimlessly, even if you bump into them. Don't worry, just take the damage they deal.

The dangerous ones are the most lethal monsters, and they live deep in dungeons.

The aggro mechanic is important to understand. Monsters normally roam aimlessly, even if you bump into them. But if you attack an enemy or cast a debuff on it, you aggro it. That means you get its attention and it will try to attack you back.

The behavioral pattern of most enemies is to attack by trying to run into you over and over again.

The best strategy against these persistent attackers is simply to attack them repeatedly. Your attacks usually have enough knockback to keep them in place.

Sometimes, as a dodge tactic, you will need to jump over them to avoid their attacks entirely.

For the full details, check out the complete list at MapleStory/Monsters/Complete list.

Remember, aggro works both ways. Stay safe and keep attacking.

Here's something worth knowing about how children learn to talk. Most of us pick up spoken language in our first few years. When a child can't hear well, that affects two things: the ability to speak, and the ability to understand what other people say.

A severe hearing deficit often goes unnoticed at first. By the time parents realize their child is deaf, communication may already have broken down at home, and the child's social skills may have suffered. A child raised in a Deaf community, where people sign rather than speak, avoids much of this (see our article on Deaf Culture).

That's why many developed countries screen newborns for hearing loss. The goal is to catch a deaf child early, before that child grows up isolated in a hearing family without anyone realizing it. Sign language is a complete way to communicate. Reading is different. Most writing systems represent the sounds of words with symbols, so learning to read still depends on understanding speech.

Consider the difference. Someone who heard well enough in childhood to learn speech and reading keeps that reading ability even if hearing later fades to the point where voices are inaudible. Someone who never heard well enough to learn to speak rarely becomes a proficient reader (see [4]). The evidence points one way: identify hearing impairment early, and a child with very insensitive hearing has a real chance of learning spoken language. Listening matters for learning a second language, too.

If this raises questions, write to us. We're happy to talk it through.

Transduction is how physical and chemical signals become neural impulses. In the nervous system, it is the basic process of translating stimuli into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, specialized sensory receptors take physical or chemical inputs and turn them into electrical impulses that travel to the brain.

The visual system shows this clearly. In the retina, rod and cone cells connect the physical environment to neural communication. Light strikes these photoreceptors and triggers a conformational change in the protein rhodopsin. That molecular shift starts a cascade of events that alters the electrochemical gradient of the photoreceptor. The gradient drops, and so do the electrical signals sent to the brain. More light hitting the photoreceptor means fewer electrical impulses. Your brain reads that pattern and decodes the visual world.

Mobile Gaming: The Next Evolution of Co-Creation

If you make games, pay attention to what mobile internet is doing to storytelling. Portable, location-aware interfaces are changing how electronic games work, and they carry on a decades-long effort to turn the player into a co-author working beside the original designers.

Here's what's new: location-aware interfaces let players pull real places into their gameworld, and push the gameworld back out into the street. No other interactive media has done that. Mobile games also abandon linear narratives. Instead, they build cooperative storytelling on what you, the player, actually experience in a place.

The "author-player" idea is old. Mobile games are not. They extend worldmaking past the screen and into physical space, using your sensory experience of real places as a storytelling tool.

In our essay, we theorize what mobile games can do for storytelling and describe our own attempt to do it: designing and building our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.

Subject: Tips for Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), or just the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. Former industrial cities make it up: Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

About five million people live here. That is far more than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. Motorways crisscross the region, yet hitchhiking can be hard, because the minor roads form a complicated network. The main motorways are the A1, A2, and A3.

Planning to hitch here? Stay on those primary motorways. Avoid the smaller roads; almost no transit traffic uses them. Germany is generally a pleasant country for hitchhiking, but the Ruhr Area is its most unpleasant part by far. Hitching inside the Ruhr feels like hitching in a big city such as Istanbul: each city stands on its own, yet to you as a traveler they all blur into districts of one enormous city.

We hope this helps you plan a safe and enjoyable trip.

Here are the results you asked for on lung tissue volume and how aeration changed between conditions.

We calculated total lung tissue volume as: number of voxels × volume of the voxel. That applies whenever the compartment has a CT number above zero.

For ΔFRC, the change in functional residual capacity caused by PEEP withdrawal, we took the difference in total gas volume of the whole lung between PEEP and ZEEP. Alveolar derecruitment was the same difference, but only in poorly aerated and nonaerated regions.

We also measured gas volume lost to PEEP withdrawal in the normally aerated regions alone, defined as CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

Last, following reference [21], we classified each patient's lung morphology as diffuse, patchy, or lobar, based on how CT attenuations were distributed at ZEEP.
